minute_key: kline open time (ms since epoch, UTC); the minute [t, t+60000) owns t and does not own t+60000
boundary_rule: No minute before prospective_from is scientific evidence; minutes before it are engineering data and are excluded from every scientific report. prospective_from is the first UTC midnight after the recorder has completed one full hour of recording; it is written once by the recorder's first run, committed in a follow-up pull request, and is immutable thereafter. While it is null the boundary has not been fixed and no minute recorded under this contract is scientific evidence. The campaign start instant is named separately by the forward protocol and must be at or after prospective_from plus the review period.

sealed_regions_inherited.p4_hold: the gen1 hold-out region, retired unread by data/research/p4_holdout_ledger.json; no generation reopens it
sealed_regions_inherited.styx: the gen1 sealed test region, from the sealed instant in nn/research_contracts/btc-usdt-1h-gen1.json onward; it is a repository non-read seal with a hindsight-era ceiling, not prospective blind evidence, and it stays sealed

checksum_scheme: SHA-256 over the gzipped raw event file and over the normalized Parquet bytes, recorded in the day manifest and the day metadata. The identity of a normalized day is the value-level digest chimera.recorder-minutes/1, taken over a domain prefix, a canonical header naming the market and its columns, the row count, and then per column a null mask followed by the values as fixed-width little-endian bytes; it is a function of the published numbers and of nothing else, so a re-encoding, a different compression, a different row-group layout or a different pyarrow version cannot move it, and changing one published number does.
coverage_rule: Required streams come in two index kinds and are counted in different units. Minute-indexed: um.kline_1m, um.markPrice, um.bookTicker, spot.kline_1m. Settlement-indexed: um.funding. For each UTC day D and each minute-indexed required stream s: published_minutes(s, D) is the set of minutes of D present in the Binance daily archive for s; captured_minutes(s, D) is the set of minutes of D present in the recorder's normalized file for s whose values agree with the archive within tolerance; published_coverage(s, D) = |captured intersect published| / |published|; wallclock_coverage(s, D) = |captured| / 1440. For um.funding: schedule_established(D) is true when a funding schedule source covering the whole of D has been fetched under the acquisition rules, verified against its .CHECKSUM companion and parsed, and false when that object is absent, unverified, unparseable or covers only part of D; it is a fact about the evidence and never about the venue. scheduled_settlements(D) is defined only when schedule_established(D): the settlements of D that source lists (three, at the eight-hour cadence in force at the time of writing; the count is read from the source and never assumed), and it may be empty, an established empty set meaning the source says no settlement was scheduled for D. captured_settlements(D) is the subset present in the recorder's settlements file agreeing exactly on settlement time, rate and markPrice. funding_complete(D) is schedule_established(D) and every settlement in scheduled_settlements(D) being present in captured_settlements(D). There is no settlement ratio and no settlement denominator: funding_complete is a quantifier over an established set and not a quotient, so a day whose established schedule is empty is funding-complete because the universal holds over the empty set, and 0 / 0 is never evaluated; schedule_established(D), |scheduled_settlements(D)| and |captured_settlements(D)| are reported as three separate values. um.funding has no wallclock coverage: it is not divided by 1440 and the 0.990 minute-stream outage threshold does not apply to it. A day passes when both hold: (1) published_coverage(s, D) >= 0.995 for every minute-indexed required stream, and (2) funding_complete(D), the day's funding schedule established and every settlement it lists captured with exact agreement. wallclock_coverage is reported beside (1) for the minute-indexed streams; a day whose wallclock_coverage < 0.990 on any minute-indexed required stream is flagged RECORDER_OUTAGE even if it passes, and three flagged days in a window fail the gate. A missing or disagreeing scheduled settlement is not a flag and fails the day outright. Three funding cases are kept apart in the record: a source establishing that no settlement was scheduled for D makes the day funding-complete with nothing for the recorder to miss, and the zero is recorded so it is visible; a schedule that could not be established is not a zero, is never recorded as one, makes funding_complete(D) false and is reported FUNDING_SCHEDULE_UNAVAILABLE, which is not a RECORDER_OUTAGE flag and does not enter the three-flagged-days count; a scheduled settlement that is missing or disagrees fails the day outright. The gate passes when 30 consecutive UTC days pass, counted from the first passing day at or after prospective_from; any day that does not pass, whether it failed or could not be judged, resets the count to zero, and the streak is recomputed from the reconciliation records every time the gate is evaluated, so a day whose schedule source appears later takes its real verdict when the reconciliation is run again for it. No price, return, funding flow, basis, profit or other economic quantity is computed by any recorder tool: settlement agreement is an equality check on published values.
reconciliation_rule: Once per UTC day, for day D-2: fetch the daily kline archives for um and spot and the monthly funding archive from data.binance.vision with their .CHECKSUM companions, under the acquisition rules already in nn.p13_acquisition (assert_allowed_url, parse_checksum_companion, path-keyed cache) and the readers in nn.p13_sources (read_kline_object, per-file epoch unit resolution); compare, minute by minute, the recorder's normalized open, high, low, close, volume and taker-buy base against the archive with relative tolerance 1e-9, the parity tolerance nn.multiclock already uses; compare funding settlements (time, rate, markPrice) exactly; write reconciliation/YYYY-MM-DD.json recording minutes compared, agreeing, disagreeing (listed), present only in the archive, present only in the recorder, the published-minute count that is the denominator of the coverage gate, and, because the funding condition of the coverage rule is evaluated from these records, whether the day's funding schedule was established and the settlements it lists when it was; never modify the recorder's files, because a disagreement is a finding and not a repair. Mark-price and index-price daily archives are reconciled the same way for the per-minute close, and the per-minute high only when the archive carries it.
recorder_version_policy: The recorder's source identity (nn.source_identity.source_identity: scheme, revision, dirty, source_digest), the Python and library versions, and a hostname hash are recorded on every day manifest, together with the contract id, the contract hash and the boundary state in force when the day was written. Any change to this contract creates a new file with a supersedes field; data recorded under the old contract keeps its hash on every manifest, and one campaign never mixes contracts.
description: Prospective, forward-only market data for the Binance USD-M BTCUSDT perpetual and Binance spot BTCUSDT, recorded from public endpoints with no credentials. Nothing under this contract has been acquired: the recorder's network layer is a later change, prospective_from is unset, and no minute of it is scientific evidence.
